title: Leaves Vietnam, sick — medical evacuation
description: Larry's year in Vietnam ended with a medical evacuation. By his account, Captain Geutler came for him on the mountain and dropped off Sgt. Weaver; back at the base a medic told him he had yellow jaundice; and he was moved by stages — to Cholon, then to Subic Bay in the Philippines, then to the Army hospital at Camp Zama, Japan. He was in and out of consciousness along the way. His DD-214 bears out that he left Vietnam as a patient: his last duty assignment was as a patient held on the rolls of the Army medical command in Japan. The day he left and the stops along the way are his memory; no travel or clinical record has been seen.
researchNotes: 2026-09-14: made distinct from the Camp Zama entry (1965-fall-japan-medical-command), which covers his time as a patient in Japan; this entry is leaving Vietnam. Confidence raised to strongly-supported to match it, for the part both rest on: the DD-214 (cited) shows he finished his service on a medical holding detachment in Japan, which only a patient is on, and box 27 reads NONE for wounds. The dates and route are his memory and are rated by datePrecision, not by the badge. His accounts: giscus-stories-c18259364 (2026-09-02, transcribed: Geutler, Weaver, the medic trailer, Cholon, Subic Bay, Camp Zama), giscus-stories-c18006833 (2026-08-13, jaundice, "medivac out a couple days later"), giscus-stories-c18118868 (2026-08-22, the Philippines), 2026-09-03-phone-camp-zama-date (paraphrase, Camp Zama "may have been 9/3/1965"). displayDate and sortDate come from working his chain back from that date; the derivation, and why no day counts render, are in research/events/medevac-chain-1965.md. The AMEDD history's general 1965 route via Clark AB is not cited here: he names Subic Bay. Record paths not yet searched: NPRC clinical records (Subic Bay and Camp Zama by name). Ledger #1, #7, #10.
